Home › Nintendo Switch 2 Nintendo Announces 2026 Black Friday Sale, Including $50 Switch 2 Bundle Discount
 Look forward to discounts on Switch 2 games and more.
 By  Robert Anderson Updated : Nov 12, 2026 2:57pm UTC Add IGN on Google 0 9 Nintendo has officially announced details for its 2026 Black Friday sale , including a brand-new offer on Switch 2 consoles, $20 off MSRP on select Nintendo Switch 2 games, and more.
 The sale will start on Nov. 22, and will headline with a $50 discount on Nintendo Switch 2's Mario Kart World console bundle . With an MSRP of $549.99, that brings it down to $499.99.
 Not Live Yet! Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle
 1 Deal available from November 22, 2026. $549.99 save 9% $499.99 at Amazon The sale will last through Nov.29, but Nintendo has also confirmed that the Switch 2 bundle offer will extend through Dec. 5, offering fans a bit more time to secure the deal.
 We have a few confirmed games that will be included in the sale so far: Donkey Kong Bananza, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, Kirby AirRiders, Super Mario Galaxy 1+2, and Super Mario Party Jamboree. As mentioned, these will be $20 off MSRP and start at $39.99 while the sale is on. 
 Don't get ahead of yourself, however, as while the $39.99 price sounds great, it is more than likely Donkey Kong Bananza will be $49.99 for Switch 2, as its current MSRP in the US is still $69.99. 
 Nintendo has also confirmed that Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target, GameStop, and the official Nintendo Store will carry these offers during the Black Friday sales at each respective retailer.
 Nintendo's 2026 Black Friday sale includes $20 off Switch games As a reminder, earlier this year, Nintendo announced a price rise for the Switch 2 in the US and other international markets. In the US, this increased the price from $449.99 to $499.99 in September 2026.
 Following this, Nintendo also revealed its new Switch 2 bundles , priced at $549.99, including either Mario Kart World or Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. These bundles also include a three-month membership to Nintendo Switch Online, which in total brings savings of $37.98, at least according to Nintendo.
 Now with the aforementioned Black Friday discount applied, savings are closer to $88 in total for the Mario Kart bundle , while the Switch Sports Resort bundle will stay at $529.99.
 This is the first official discount the Nintendo Switch 2 has received since it first launch in June 2025.
 Nintendo Switch 2 will be $50 off for Black Friday. We saw a surprise discount on a similar Mario Kart World bundle during Black Friday last year , but as far as we're aware, this was led by retailers like Walmart and Amazon, rather than Nintendo itself. 
 Down to $449.99, this included both the Switch 2 console and Mario Kart, but didn't include the Nintendo Switch Online membership. 
 While the Switch 2 is on sale in the US this year, it's effectively wiping away the $50 price hike from September. Whether or not you see that as a deal is your own prerogative. 
 We've already seen some fairly good Switch 2 deals in the run up to Black Friday as well, including one giant discount at AliExpress , and another for new customers at Woot . But, if you'd prefer to wait it out for the official deal from Nintendo, that's a reasonable move as well.
 Do you plan on doing your shopping before Black Friday this year?
 Yes! No, I'm going to wait Only if the deal is really good Answer See Results Should You Wait for Black Friday on November 27?
 Black Friday deals are more confusing than ever these days. Most retailers spend November teasing limited-time offers, but the reality is that the deepest discounts rarely arrive until about a week before what I like to call "Black Friday proper."
 Having tracked Nintendo sales for years, one thing is clear: once a Switch deal hits (like it is on November 22), it usually sticks for the rest of the sale. That means the prices you see now on consoles, games, and accessories are very likely the ones that’ll hold through to December. If you’ve been holding out for a solid deal, there’s no need to wait any longer.
 These offers are reliable, worthwhile, and unlikely to get any better. Grab the games and hardware you’ve had your eye on, there’s no risk of Black Friday regret, only the satisfaction of finally getting exactly what you wanted at a price that makes sense.
